blocks.text: The Philippine housing backlog is estimated to reach 3.7 million units between 2022 and 2028, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). Meanwhile, housing production from 2022 to the end of 2025 totaled only about 477,000 units, based on statements from the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD). In other words, by the end of last year, only 13 percent of the backlog had been addressed, highlighting the need for more housing units. Ironically, when you look at the Metro Manila condominium market, you see significant unsold inventory, reaching 80,000 units in Q3 2026. The issue is not just […]...
